I couldn't compile the change, so it is untested. The offline Maven build failed because `maven-build-cache-extension` isn't cached locally.

I added a target-user check to `getCredentialOfferState()` in `OID4VCAuthorizationDetailsProcessor`, next to the existing target-client check. If the offer has a `targetUserId` and it doesn't match the authenticated user, the method now throws an `IllegalStateException`. This covers both offer lookup paths: the pre-authorized offer attribute and `issuer_state`. It runs during authorization, before any `IssuedVerifiableCredential` record is created for the wrong user. A stolen targeted offer is therefore rejected up front, and it no longer matters that the refresh provider nulls `credentialsOfferId`. `UserModel` was already imported.

I didn't run any tests or add new ones. Offers with no `targetUserId` are unaffected.

I didn't use the axiomengine graph for this. The hook reported no graph built for this repo, and I went straight to grep.
